content.thinking: Checking the listIssues filter input to see if it supports listing issues assigned to a specific user.
The activity database schema needs an action enum.
Checking the webhook for issue assignment events.
Checking the pagination limit for listing all issues.
Checking the notify logic to see how actor self-skip is handled.
Checking emails for kind union and manifest scripts that list events.

Checking whether assignIssue emits an assigned event when the assigneeId matches the current non-null assignee. The existing behavior will be preserved.

Unassigning when the previous assignee is already null will skip the database write and emit nothing. The remaining cases follow standard unassigned and assigned event rules.

The member service will list issues by assignee after archiving a member and call setIssueAssignee to unassign each one. Using the issue repository directly is permitted. Calling assignIssue instead would re-check permissions and scope, which is acceptable.

Direct repository calls and emits are preferred over assignIssue to avoid permission failures mid-loop. Archived issues keep their assignee, but listIssues excludes them by default. The member service will paginate through issues by assignee in batches of 100, unassigning each one and emitting an issue.unassigned event.

The search listener should also subscribe to issue.unassigned events. This keeps the search index fresh when assignees change, matching the existing subscription pattern for issue.updated.
Checking email rendering to exhaustively record the kinds.
The notification preferences page might seed all kinds.

SQLite text enums in Drizzle are app-level. No migration is needed if no check constraint exists.

I'll update the constant. I'll add a listener for `issue.unassigned` so clearing an assignee still reindexes search. I won't add missing issue events like `issue.assigned` or `issue.updated`.

I'll suppress the `updated` event when `assignIssue` sets an assignee to null if it was already null. I'll unassign issues after the `member.removed` event so the membership change is recorded first.
Applying all edits now. Checking activity-service for an issue.
